items.reason: Identifies strategy shutdown destroying the factory-owned pool reused after rebalance. The different claimed commit consequence does not change the shared lifecycle bug.
Identifies the commit scan requiring every integer offset and treating legitimate Kafka offset gaps as blockers.
Identifies unbounded worker queues and missing backpressure, allowing unlimited memory growth when processing falls behind.
Identifies the shared factory-owned pool being shut down by a strategy and then reused after rebalance.
Identifies failed offsets being completed in finally despite the successful-processing guarantee. Suggesting a documentation change instead does not change the underlying problem.
Identifies the backpressure guarantee contradicted by unbounded queues and unconditional submission.

Identifies the error-handling test asserting no commit despite claiming errors should not block commits, and requests a positive commit assertion. Its timing observation also explains why that contradictory assertion passes.
Identifies unconditional completion in finally making failed messages committable, contrary to the documented success-only guarantee.
Identifies strategy lifecycle methods shutting down the shared pool that subsequent strategies reuse after rebalance.
Identifies reuse of the shut-down factory-owned pool after rebalance, with enqueue failures swallowed and unprocessed offsets marked complete.
Identifies the scan start jumping over a missing offset after committed offsets are pruned, allowing a later commit cycle to cross the gap.
